newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says he agrees in principle with the idea of holding direct prime ministerial elections, but insists that more study will be needed to determine if such a drastic change is really necessary. The Constitution Drafting Assembly has reluctantly rejected mounting public calls for direct prime ministerial elections, saying the country is not ready for a drastic revamp of its political structure. (THE NATION)

- A villager in Kanchanaburi province will today file a lawsuit against the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) which he says has cleared his farmland to facilitate its gas pipeline project without his consent. He will also file another lawsuit against Thong Pha Phum district police for negligence. PTT has begun constructing its pipeline after its environmental impact assessment was approved by the National Environment Board last week. (BANGKOK POST)

- The prime minister has played down opposition criticism of his administration and denies it is tapping Democrat members' phones. Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says the opposition is doing its duty in making criticisms but only its leader's comments carry weight. (BANGKOK POST)

- Small finance companies are not so eager to jump on the merger bandwagon being encouraged by the Bank of Thailand (BOT) as a means of surviving the challenge of competition and future liberalisation. The central bank's merger criteria promotes the merging of small financial institutions, but it also discrimiates against them if they refuse to take the BOT's advice and merge. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Local pay-television operators are discussing a plan to set up a joint venture to strengthen their bargaining power with foreign programme suppliers and thus reduce their costs. Executives of Thai Sky TV and Universal Cable TV have met recently to discuss the possibility and reached a common understanding that buying programming separately is quite costly. (BANGKOK POST)
